fatal_errors: The proposed alloy system and processing intervention are unrelated to the target composition-screening and VEC/modulus strategy in Nb-Mo-Ta-V-W.
Young’s modulus, one of the requested properties, is neither predicted nor included in the falsification measurements.
No quantitative improvement relative to a defined state-of-the-art baseline is specified.
The claimed formation of coherent nanoparticles in aged CoCrFeMnNi is unsupported by cited prior evidence or a phase-selection rationale.
The proposed comparison changes directional solidification and aging simultaneously, so it cannot distinguish magnetic-field, grain-structure, and precipitation effects.
explanation: The hypothesis addresses the broad goal of improving structural HEA properties and offers a nominally testable processing comparison, but it does not reconstruct the target methodology, material system, conditions, mechanism, or quantitative result. The target used validated composition-based modulus estimates and VEC to screen refractory Nb-Mo-Ta-V-W compositions, producing Nb15Mo2.5Ta40V40W2.5 with about 35.7% compressive fracture strain while retaining high strength. By contrast, the generated proposal gives no evidence that 10 T directional solidification followed by 500 °C aging will produce coherent precipitates or simultaneously improve strength and ductility in CoCrFeMnNi. Its baseline and expected effect are vague, and the experiment omits modulus and lacks factorial controls. It is therefore an unsupported alternative rather than a supported reconstruction.
